\section{CNF encoding and its soundness}\label{fin:sec:encoding}

\subsection{Primary variables and structural clauses}

For every unordered pair \(e=\{u,v\}\in\binom V2\), a primary variable
\(x_e\) records whether \(e\in E(F)\).  The \(4950\) primary variables are
numbered in lexicographic pair order.  Crucially, variables exist for all
original nonedges; those variables are absent from the deletion counter and
are not fixed false.

Triangle-freeness is encoded without separation: for every \(a<b<c\), the
formula contains
\[
  \neg x_{ab}\lor\neg x_{ac}\lor\neg x_{bc}.
\]
There are exactly \(\binom{100}{3}=161700\) such clauses.

For every installed set \(S\in\binom V{18}\), the formula contains the
positive hitting clause
\[
  C_S=\bigvee_{e\in\binom S2}x_e.                 \tag{F4.1}\label{fin:main:eq:4-1}
\]
It has \(\binom{18}{2}=153\) distinct primary literals.  Every graph with
independence number below \(18\) satisfies \(C_S\).  We install only a finite
selected bank \(\cB_i\), not all \(\binom{100}{18}\) clauses.  Consequently,
\(\Phi_i\) is a relaxation of the exact Ramsey branch.  This is the useful
direction: unsatisfiability of the relaxation implies unsatisfiability of the
exact branch.

\subsection{Exact deletion counter}

In branch \(i\), let
\[
  L_i=\bigl(\neg x_e:e\in E(H)\setminus\{f_i\}\bigr)
\]
be the ordered list obtained by restricting the lexicographic pair order to
the seed edges other than \(f_i\).  The list has \(826\) literals.  A PySAT
sequential-counter equality encoding
implements
\[
  \sum_{\ell\in L_i}[\ell\text{ is true}]=5.      \tag{F4.2}\label{fin:main:eq:4-2}
\]
We use the standard sequential counter of Sinz~\cite{Sinz2005}.  The concrete
generator is exposed by PySAT~\cite{Ignatiev2018}; its semantics is not used as
an unchecked black box.

For completeness, define the irredundant sequential schema explicitly.  Given
signed literals \(z_0,\ldots,z_{n-1}\) and \(1\le q\le n-2\), introduce
\(y_{r,j}\) for \(0\le r<q\) and \(0\le j<n-q\), and let
\(\operatorname{SC}_{\le q}(z)\) contain
\begin{align*}
 \neg z_j\lor y_{0,j}\quad
   &(0\le j<n-q),\\
 \neg y_{r,j}\lor y_{r,j+1}\quad
   &(0\le r<q,\ 0\le j<n-q-1),\\
 \neg z_{j+r+1}\lor\neg y_{r,j}\lor y_{r+1,j}\quad
   &(0\le r<q-1,\ 0\le j<n-q),\\
 \neg z_{j+q}\lor\neg y_{q-1,j}\quad
   &(0\le j<n-q).
\end{align*}

\begin{lemma}[Sequential-counter projection semantics]
\label{fin:lem:seqcounter-projection}
For every assignment of the primary variables,
\[
 \exists y\ \operatorname{SC}_{\le q}(z,y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}[z_j\text{ is true}]\le q.       \tag{F4.3}\label{fin:main:eq:4-3}
\]
Consequently, for \(n=826\),
\[
 \operatorname{SC}_{\le821}(\neg z)\land
 \operatorname{SC}_{\le5}(z)
\]
has an auxiliary extension if and only if exactly five members of \(z\) are
true.  The budget-five block \(\operatorname{SC}_{\le4}(z)\) has an auxiliary
extension if and only if at most four members are true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Suppose first that at most \(q\) input literals are true.  Assign
\(y_{r,j}=1\) exactly when at least \(r+1\) of
\(z_0,\ldots,z_{j+r}\) are true.  The first clause family records the first
threshold crossing.  The second propagates an attained threshold to a longer
prefix.  In the third family, truth of both \(z_{j+r+1}\) and \(y_{r,j}\)
raises the prefix count from at least \(r+1\) to at least \(r+2\).  The last
family cannot be violated, because such a violation would exhibit \(q+1\)
true inputs.  This gives the required auxiliary extension.

Conversely, induction on \(r\) shows that the clauses force \(y_{r,j}=1\)
whenever at least \(r+1\) of \(z_0,\ldots,z_{j+r}\) are true.  For \(r=0\),
use the first clause at the position of a true input and then the propagation
clauses.  For the induction step, let \(p\) be the position of the
\((r+1)\)-st true input and put \(j'=p-r\).  The induction hypothesis forces
\(y_{r-1,j'}\); the third family, together with \(z_p\), forces \(y_{r,j'}\),
and propagation reaches \(y_{r,j}\).  If \(q+1\) inputs were true, let \(p\)
be the position of the \((q+1)\)-st and put \(j=p-q\).  The preceding argument
forces \(y_{q-1,j}\), while the last family forbids its conjunction with
\(z_p\), a contradiction.  This proves \eqref{fin:main:eq:4-3}.  Applying \eqref{fin:main:eq:4-3} to \(z\) and
to its \(826\) complements gives respectively the upper and lower sides of
the equality claim; the at-most-four claim is the direct case \(q=4\).
\end{proof}

In the exact-five DIMACS block, the complement counter at bound \(821\) comes
first and has \(4105\) auxiliary variables and \(7394\) clauses; the positive
counter at bound \(5\) has another \(4105\) auxiliaries and \(9026\) clauses.
Thus the equality block has \(8210\) auxiliary variables and \(16420\) clauses,
ending at variable \(13160\).  The checker
\path{routes/finite/check_r3_18_seqcounter.py} does not import or call PySAT's
cardinality generator.  It independently generates the four clause families,
compares all six actual counter blocks clause-for-clause in their canonical
literal order, checks their digests and variable ranges, and constructs the
prefix-threshold auxiliary assignment from the proof above.  Exhaustive
small-instance tests enumerate both primary and auxiliary assignments and
verify both directions of the projected at-most and equality semantics.

Thus
\[
 \Phi_i=\Bigl(\bigwedge_{a<b<c}
   (\neg x_{ab}\lor\neg x_{ac}\lor\neg x_{bc})\Bigr)
 \land \operatorname{Card}_{=5}(L_i)
 \land \neg x_{f_i}
 \land \bigwedge_{S\in\cB_i} C_S.                \tag{F4.4}\label{fin:main:eq:4-4}
\]

\begin{proposition}[CNF soundness]\label{fin:prop:cnf-sound}
For each \(i\), every graph \(F\in\cF\) with \(d_H(F)=6\) and
\(f_i\notin E(F)\) induces a primary assignment that extends to a model of
\(\Phi_i\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The triangle block holds by triangle-freeness.  The fixed unit holds by the
branch premise.  Since \(f_i\) is one of exactly six missing input edges,
exactly five literals in \(L_i\) are true; \cref{fin:lem:seqcounter-projection}
supplies an auxiliary assignment.  Each \(S\in\cB_i\) contains a
present pair because \(\alpha(F)<18\), so every \(C_S\) holds.  No condition
was imposed on an original nonedge except through triangle and hitting
clauses, hence arbitrary additions remain represented.
\end{proof}
